context.title: Hearts Burning on the Road
context.summary: Women find the tomb empty and angels announce the resurrection. Jesus walks with two disciples to Emmaus, explains the Scriptures, and is recognized in breaking bread. He appears to the eleven, eats with them, and ascends near Bethany.
context.background: Emmaus was about seven miles from Jerusalem (v. 13); its exact location is uncertain. The apostles first dismiss the women's report as 'idle tales' (v. 11). Luke's Gospel ends where it began, in the temple, with the disciples praising God (v. 53).

customs.note: At a meal the host took bread, gave thanks, broke it and handed it out. The guest Jesus takes the host's role.

watchFor: 'Did not our heart burn within us?' (v. 32).
Jesus says Moses, the prophets and the psalms all speak of him (v. 44).
'Ye are witnesses' (v. 48) sets up the book of Acts.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.).

people.name: Joanna
people.summary: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Cleophas
people.summary: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Emmaus
places.summary: Hot baths, a village “three-score furlongs” from jerusalem, where our Lord had an interview with two of his disciples on the day of his resurrection (Luke 24:13).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

places.name: Bethany
places.summary: A village on the south-eastern slope of the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:1), about 2 miles east of Jerusalem, on the road to Jericho. It derived its name from the number of palm-trees which grew there.

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Resurrection and Ascension
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 28:1 – John 20:31. People: Jesus, Mary, Salome, Thomas. Place: Jerusalem, mount of Olives, sea of Galilee.
